person: New mother in Nigeria (Rivers State), nuclear or extended household
situation: A new mother in Nigeria's Rivers State is expected to follow community cord-care norms: 76.7% of mothers in her region use methylated spirit, 17.6% petroleum jelly, 13.8% herbal preparations, and 17.7% hot water — all practices that deviate from WHO dry-care guidance.
trigger: The mother's own upbringing and community norms dictate the cord-care substances; a 2025 survey of 232 mothers found these practices are prevalent across the state.
context: Rivers State, Nigeria (2025 survey, 232 mothers). 76.7% methylated spirit, 40% chlorhexidine, 15.9% toothpaste, 17.6% petroleum jelly, 13.8% herbal preparations, 12.5% breastmilk, 17.7% hot water. These are not 'mistakes' — they are the default community practice, passed down through generations.
behaviour: Mother follows community norm (methylated spirit or herbal preparation)
Mother may have been told by clinic to use dry care but community practice overrides
Mother may not have access to chlorhexidine even though 40% use it (availability gap)

failed_attempts.tried: Mother may have tried dry care but family/community pressure overruled

constraint: Community practice is the default; clinical guidance is aspirational; access to recommended products (chlorhexidine) is limited; cultural authority favors traditional practice.
thought: Everyone in my community uses methylated spirit. The clinic said dry care but that's not how we do it here.
fear: Deviation from community norm; being seen as ignoring tradition; the cord not healing properly without intervention.
emotional_stake: Identity — following community practice is part of being a 'good mother' in this context.
exact_language: 76.7% methylated spirit, 40% chlorhexidine, 15.9% toothpaste, 17.6% petroleum jelly, 13.8% herbal preparations, 12.5% breastmilk, 17.7% hot water.
desired_change: A culturally grounded explanation of why dry care works, framed within (not against) the mother's identity as a good mother in her community.

evidence_source.excerpt: 76.7% methylated spirit, 40% chlorhexidine, 15.9% toothpaste, 17.6% petroleum jelly, 13.8% herbal preparations, 12.5% breastmilk, 17.7% hot water.
evidence_source.context: Cross-sectional survey of 232 mothers in Rivers State, Nigeria (2025). Documents prevalence of non-WHO cord-care practices.

relationships: Same West African traditional-substance pattern as CRF-PPL-CORD-CARE-006 (Ghana, grandmother-driven); Nigeria variant is community-norm-driven
Same Nigerian context as CRF-PPL-CORD-CARE-005 but Rivers State is a specific regional variant with documented prevalence data
